Hello Petra, I see you decided to wear something from Brigid rather than your uniform today.
That's a new look, Lysithea. If I didn't know better I'd say you aged a few years since yesterday.
Lysithea, it's good to see you taking a break from your studies. I admire your dedication, but I worry sometimes that you're going to burn yourself out.
Rhea!? Wait no... My apologies, Miss. I mistook you for someone else. (The resemblance is uncanny though...)
Bernadetta? I'm pleased to see you out of your room, but this is the last place I expected to find you.
Ah, Petra! This is a surprise, though hardly an unpleasant one.
Galatea, was it? No relation to House Galatea of Faerghus, I presume?
You're here too, Hilda? I hope this means that you finished your chores, and not that you foisted them on somebody else.
Ignatz, is that you? Are you here scouting models for your paintings?
Leonie? This is a pleasant surprise, I thought you generally preferred contests of a more athletic nature.
It's rare that I get time away from my duties like this; let alone the opportunity to spend it in the company of those from beyond Fódlan. I'm certain that this will prove an enlightening experience.
To be invited to a game of strip poker was surprising, but I've committed, so I shall give my all.
It appears we have a full table. Shall we begin?
Don't worry about Bernadetta. Running away screaming is kind of... her thing.
(Monica...) Hm? It's nothing. Forget about it.
Just to be clear, you are here willingly. Right, Bernadetta? As your house leader it is my responsibility to ensure my classmates aren't being coerced into these kinds of things.
I have to ask, what brought you here Bernadetta? To put it bluntly, this isn't the sort of game I'd normally envision someone as timid as yourself playing.
So what are you doing here of all places, Bernadetta? I'm struggling to think of an activity less aligned with your preferences than strip poker.
Who'd have thought we'd run into another "~player~" here?
I was baffled when I heard Bernadetta, of all people, was here. I suppose it makes sense it was just someone else with the same name.
You're Petra, are you? I have a friend with that name. Perhaps I should arrange a match with her sometime.
Hm... What are the odds of meeting another "Edelgard" here?
Byleth is it? How strange to meet someone with the same name as my teacher here.
Well, you may not be my Hubert, but I hope we can get along all the same.
You're going by "~player~"!? Is that really your name, or is this some perverse attempt at humor!?
Here's hoping this Linhardt can stay awake the whole game.
Another Caspar? You don't seem nearly as loud as the one I know.
Ah, another Ferdinand. You only need to tell me your name the once, thank you.
Oh. You aren't the Dorothea I know. Pity, I was looking forward to playing against her.
This city is undeniably a marvel, but the streets hardly seem an appropriate setting for a game like this.
This place is so noisy and crowded, should we really be playing here?
This throne room is rather cozy compared to the one in the Imperial Palace.
Is this a classroom? It's rather sterile compared to the ones at the Officers Academy.
What a magnificent city. It reminds me of Enbarr in some ways.
I love the scent of the forest, it makes me feel so far away from all of my other commitments.
Do you enjoy the sound of the water? I find it tends to bring up bad memories.
(This pool seems rather deep... I'd best be careful, I'd hate for someone to have to rescue me if I fell in.)
The beach... I'd prefer to stay away from the surf, if you don't mind.
(What an adorable plush I'll have to see if I can discretely figure out where to acquire one...)
Must we play here? This place looks liable to attract rats... and other vermin.
I will never falter; even if my opponents are the gods themselves.
Surely there is a more appropriate venue for our game. Are you certain nobody will come in here?
Brace yourself, for I have no intention of going easy on you.
While I'm more partial to board games, I'm no stranger to cards. Underestimate me at your own peril.
Keep your wits about you, or this game will be over before it begins.
One card is all I need.
Only the two, thank you.
Not awful, but it could be better. I'll take three.
I'll only be holding onto this one.
These are absolutely worthless. I'll trade all five.
No need to fix what isn't broken. I'll keep these cards.
One step at a time...
I'll take my chances with this hand as it is.
Ah, a lucky break. I don't need to swap.
Think this through.
How best to use these cards?
Just one card, if you please.
This card is the weak link in my hand.
Hmm... this has potential. Two cards.
I see...Maybe if I draw those two...
Three cards will suffice.
Dealer, I require three cards.
There's not much I can do with this. Four cards.
Ugh... Four cards please.
Unbelievable. Give me a fresh hand.
This hand is not remotely salvageable. Give me five new cards.
An auspicious start.
One of us must fall before the others. Which of you will it be?
With these cards, I will seize victory!
If one truly seeks victory, then they must seize it with their own hands. They cannot sit idle and simply wait for it to come to them.
On the battlefield, in the classroom, or at the poker table, I must strive for excellence in all things.
I do hope you aren’t manipulating the cards to try and curry favor with me, dealer. I have no desire for special treatment, least of all when it involves malfeasance.
No mercy.
I don’t envy you, going up against this hand.
So many different people, from such a diversity of worlds, patronize this place… I’m keen to see what new perspectives I may discover here.
A good hand, at least.
I’m safe for now, but I must not grow complacent.
The world can be a cold, and unfair place, but sometimes you hit upon a stroke of luck regardless.
If I had known I was going to have luck like this, I would have stripped my gloves instead.
To walk the path before me I must outwit even death.
This game may have nothing to do with my ambitions, but I give it my all just the same.
The Adrestian Princess strides forward, yielding to nothing and to no one.
Loath as I am to rely upon it, fortune has served me well this hand.

I will strip you down until you have no dignity left to cling to!
~blank~...~blank~
What? I was just trying to rally your spirits.
I so rarely get the opportunity to let my hair down like this. It’s not something I take for granted.
Hah! A hand this good deserves a fitting sobriquet. Perhaps the "Annihilator of Modesty”?
There are no miracles but those you make for yourself, and make one I shall!
Even if I’m stripped bare, I will find a way to keep pressing onward!
My physical strength may be enhanced by the power of Crests, but my fortitude and intellect are entirely my own.
I have no intention of surrendering as long as there remains the faintest hope of victory. If you seek my defeat, it will need to be total.
I wonder if Dorothea has ever played this game. It seems like the sort of thing she might be into.
There are certainly worse hands to start with.
These cards... are sufficient.
I must remain resolute. To let myself be ruled by emotion is to court disaster.
One of you must have something worse.
I'd like for this to be better, but I can't complain.
Not bad, but it would be nice to have some of Caspar’s optimism at this stage in the game.
Games are more than mere entertainment. They can train important skills too. Even this simplistic version of poker involves some level of pattern recognition and risk management.
In life, I have chosen my path and embraced an uncertain future. An uncertain hand of cards is nothing by comparison.
My situation back in Fódlan is... complicated... to say the least. This hand, by contrast, is anything but.
We have communal baths at the monastery, but I normally rise early and bathe while everybody else is still in bed. This whole endeavor is a rather novel experience for me.
You know. you rather remind me of my teacher ~player~. You're both quiet and difficult to get a read on. It's not a criticism, merely an observation.

Dorothea is a good friend but she can be a bit much at times. Once, she had the idea of an opera about me and next thing I knew she was singing a song glorifying "the mighty Edelgard". It was more than a little embarrassing.
Whatever the future may hold, I will always cherish my time at the academy and the friends I’ve made there.
Many gamblers in Fódlan swear that eating a certain type of bean makes you luckier. To the point they're actually called "Miracle Beans". It sounds like utter nonsense to me.
Normally I’d put more effort into my poker face, but this particular rule-set doesn't have much use for deception.

No matter how hard one tries to control a situation there will always be unpredictable elements at play. Being able to adapt in the heat of the moment is just as important for a leader as the ability to plan long-term.
I've done all I can. The rest is up to luck, sadly.
Capable rulers must be able to pierce the veil of deception and discern others’ true intentions. In that respect, they are not so different from gamblers.
I don't like settling for average. But average is often sufficient.
It’s unavoidable that things sometimes fall to chance. I'll simply have to wait and see how this plays out.
I wonder how my teacher would handle a situation like this?
Some like to attribute their hands to “fate” or the “will of the goddess”. I’m not so superstitious.
It’s a decent enough hand. This should pose no problems.
There is no planning ahead in a game like this; I shall simply have to take it one step at a time.
I'm off to a terrible start.
I suppose it's too much to hope that Linhardt isn't using my absence as an opportunity to shirk his responsibilities.
Do I seem stiff to you? I’m afraid I’m not well-practiced in the art of small talk.
Unacceptable. I must do better.
An underwhelming result... I will not let it happen again.
This being a game of chance, I have naturally accounted for the possibility that not every hand will go my way.
A minor setback.
This bodes poorly, but it’s nothing I can’t recover from.
If I'm being honest, I'm not looking forward to stripping, but I'm here to challenge those inhibitions.

Ugh...
Yes. My hand is terrible. Could you try not to look so pleased about it? Though... I suppose your eagerness to see me fail at this game is a compliment... in its own perverse way.
If I were feeling generous I might say that I prefer playing this hand over fighting a demonic beast. But I'm not feeling generous.
This is not what I wanted to see.
A damnable hand composition. But I will not let it shake my resolve.
I often struggle to feel at ease, there are so many things constantly weighing on my mind. Now this hand adds to the pile.
I’ll simply be thankful that this hand has no bearing on my ambitions.
I must tread carefully, I can't afford to keep taking losses.
So much for that plan.
If I lack the fortitude to handle this game, then my dreams are all for naught.
Mmgh...
Perhaps I need to rethink my tactics.
How shameful.
This is distressing, but I cannot fail here.
I may lose this battle, but the war is far from over.
Not good. But there’s nothing to be done about it now I suppose.
Don’t expect me to throw a fit about how something-or-other is beneath my station. Only fools believe they’re entitled to special treatment on account of their bloodline.
It's not that I am unaware of my foibles, but for the sake of the Empire and all of Fódlan, I must never show weakness, lest those of ill intent learn of and exploit it.
That said... Since nobody else here is from Fódlan, I feel I can afford to relax. If only a little.

state.text: Unlike me, most descendants of Crested bloodlines do not themselves bear a Crest. Many nobles are willing to do unspeakable things to ensure they have a Crested heir and thereby reinforce their house's claim of divine favor.

Though Crests may boost one's combat prowess, they do nothing for morals or skill at governing. For Fódlan to prosper, I believe we must stop venerating the Crested and allow people to rise and fall by their merits, regardless of bloodline.

case.state: I feel rather foolish for asking, but are you okay, ~msfortune~?
Please tell me I'm not the only one here with her head properly attached...

Grow up, Hilda.

condition.saying: Well, yeah, I guess. But Holst earned his reputation as a warrior and a leader himself - I think that his actual work reserves him a spot in history at least as important as where Dimitri and Edelgard got to just by being born.

case.state: For once, I agree with you Hilda. Lord Holst is an exemplary general, on par with the Empire's own Count Bergliez; not to mention living proof that Crests and Heroes' Relics are not needed to defend Fódlan's borders.

state.text: The past is a poor place to look for role models. It's necessarily full of those who adhered to outdated values.
I can't think of a single notable person in the history of Fódlan I can truly call admirable. They're all, in their own ways, responsible for the deeply unjust world we currently inhabit.

I suppose I can credit the founders of the Leicester Alliance with trying something new by breaking away from monarchy. Though in practice the aristocratic oligarchy they created serves the people no better.

Much ink has been spilled on the relationship between my ancestor Emperor Wilhelm I and Saint Seiros. Since my bloodline carries Seiros's Crest, it's even been speculated that she was the true mother of Lycaon I, Wilhelm's son and heir. It's not impossible, but I'm skeptical.
I once found Professor Manuela reading a book called the Tome of Comely Saints, which seemed to be full of that sort of thing. Seteth would likely have a conniption if he knew.

case.state: In Fódlan's history? It has to be the Battle of Tailtean Plains in Imperial Year 91. There, Saint Seiros slew King Nemesis, paving the way for Adrestia's victory in the War of Heroes and thus for the nascent Church of Seiros to reshape the land's politics and culture according to its doctrines.
The Church of Seiros has long concealed and distorted the true history of Fódlan to suit their own agenda. I personally prefer to focus on the future.

Some may think me heartless for saying it but, given the choice between a single life and the world, one must prioritize the world. Weighing lives is never easy, but making hard choices and living with them is the burden of we who choose action over complacency.

I would consider you lucky indeed if only one life stands between you and saving the world. In Fódlan, countless lives are lost each day in needless conflicts and countless others, be it due to ignorance, apathy, or privilege would sooner fight to the death than abandon that abominable paradigm.

Supernova. If you want to save anybody, you need to realize that you can't save everybody. Hard as it is to accept, meaningful victories are rarely won without sacrifice. All we can do is minimize the losses.

I'm afraid that's a discussion for another time Gwen.
(Even if others from Fódlan weren't present, my actions as the Flame Emperor would no doubt prove... controversial.)
A pleasure, Sucrose. As I believe I mentioned earlier, I'm Edelgard. Are you feeling alright? You seem quite nervous.

state.text: Indeed, I do. My retainer, Hubert, and our classmate, Ferdinand, always seem to be bickering about something or other. It's quite tiresome.

Two of the professors at the academy, Hanneman and Manuela, are like oil and water. They usually manage to maintain a degree of professionalism around us students... well... at least Hanneman does. With Manuela it depends on her sobriety.
Yes, Counts Bergliez and Hevring, the Empire's Ministers of Military Affairs and Domestic Affairs respectively. They make cabinet meetings a hassle. Somehow their sons ended up best friends though.

case.state: What kind of flowers do I like? Well, I've always been fond of carnations.

A free and equal society for the people of Fódlan, one devoid of senseless violence and suffering; a society where people are valued by merit, not bloodline. Nothing I may want for myself matters more than bringing that dream to fruition.
I always wander outside when sleep evades me. I despise being cooped up, I just have to get some fresh air.
That sounds... deeply unpleasant. I would never want to lose control of myself like that, I prefer to keep my mind sharp at all times.

So, you're the type of noble who believes her status places her above the rules, are you Amalia? Disgraceful! Be grateful I don't have my axe or I would simply cut those flowers away. But make no mistake I will best you in as many hands as it takes for you to concede defeat!
Amalia, do you think you're entitled to break the rules just because you're a princess? If I had my axe I would cut down those flowers but instead, I'll just keep beating you until you admit defeat!

Do you really think being born a princess gives you the right to cheat? Despicable. Had I my axe handy I would cut down those flowers and force you to play by the rules. Instead, I shall simply settle for besting you in cards until you have no choice but to comply!

condition.saying: I'm Critical Darling, by the way. I mean, that's my stage name, not my actual name, but you're more likely to know me by my stage name!

case.state: Not to offend, but isn't that a touch presumptuous for a stage name? Even when Dorothea went by "the Mystical Songstress" she wasn't directly telling you how she ought to be received.

I suspected as much. You really are shameless, you know that?

condition.saying: At Garreg Mach, we prefer games of strategy, not mere chance.

case.state: While I share your preference Lysithea, chance plays a role on the battlefield too. Many generals lose because they are unable to adapt to unpredictable factors, such as the weather.
Nnngh...
If it was for a brighter future for the people of Fódlan, my soul would be a small price to pay.
I'd really rather talk about anything else.

(Meeting my past self... There's every temptation to try saving her... from the scars... from the nightmares... but at what cost? Could she still do what must be done? Would she even try? Or would she simply become another noble content to let the evils of the world be.)
Personally, I think true freedom is opportunity. It's the ability to pursue your own course as far as you can, advantaged or disadvantaged only by your individual merits.

I'm afraid that's a discussion for another time Gwen.
(Even if word doesn't make it back to Fódlan, my actions as the Flame Emperor are liable to make me a pariah.)
It wasn't necessarily the largest such creature I've been involved in slaying, but I once had to kill a demonic beast on my own. Even the smallest would typically be work for a battalion or two.
Birds fly because it's what they do best, it's the niche they've made for themselves with their own abilities. To demand they do otherwise would be absurd.

There is no question that experiences can change people, Velvet. However, in my experience, many of the worst evils are not so much the product of discrete events as they are of a society structured to reward such behaviors.

(I know that look, Ayano... So, I'm not the only one here playing at being an innocent schoolgirl. Being from different worlds, I doubt whatever she's up to will interfere with my plans, but perhaps I'll have Hubert look into her, just in case.)
You're awfully quiet Komi. I hope I haven't frightened you; I am told I can be somewhat intimidating.
A game well played Bernadetta. Unfortunately, only one of us can claim victory. I'll be giving my all and I expect the same from you. No hard feelings, regardless of who wins.
(Still, Palutena looks oddly familiar, even apart from resembling Rhea, but I can't put my finger on it... Did I dream about seeing her fighting my teacher once? No... it couldn't be.)
Is that so? While magic isn't my primary focus, I do know a few fire spells I could try teaching you, if you're interested Darling.
So that's a Pokémon? What a curious creature. It's clearly no ordinary animal, yet it's quite unlike the Demonic Beasts we have in Fódlan.
Hmph... I suppose there is one arena in which you don't slack-off after all.
Oh, I adore nature! When I get time away from my duties I love to find a scenic vista and simply let myself take in my surroundings.
I do love nature. It's a pity my duties so rarely permit me the time to go exploring. I usually have to settle for a stroll through the gardens.
Fine. I'll admit you impressed me. If only because you completed a task without foisting the work on somebody else for a change.
I see... And do you do anything useful, Aqua? Or do you only deign to help mortals after they've already suffered and died?
So, you've already been made to bear a child at your age, Asuna? I suppose such cruelties aren't constrained to Fódlan's borders.
I won't stop now ~opponent~. You too must fall!
I won't stop now ~opponent~. You too must fall!
I can't help but feel a bit guilty. Even if you said it's fine, you certainly didn't come here to gaze upon marred flesh like mine. Perhaps an angle which obscures the scarring would be better?
Easy there Bernadetta, you're going to drop your cards.
Hubert is my retainer, by the way. While most people find him... unsettling... there is nobody in Fódlan I trust more.
The sun is so warm on my skin. I see why people pine for it so.
Tell me if you see any pretty flowers. Not to pluck, mind you, just to admire.

I wonder... Do you think destiny is decided at birth? I, for one, believe we can and should forge our fates with our own hands. To be so passive as to allow some invisible force to dictate our lives would be ignorant and irresponsible.
An emperor can never know too much about governance. Are there any interesting forms of government in your worlds?
I've heard that many worlds have chess. I'm quite fond of it myself, but there are only a handful of others at the monastery who can give me a real challenge. Does anyone here play?

The church's teachings generally forbid contact with non-Fódlans. Theoretically, I could be branded a heretic for being here; though the archbishop is surely smart enough to know it's not worth the political cost.

Now that I think about it, it's strange that we are able to understand one another flawlessly; even though logically speaking, our worlds' languages should be nothing alike. This place is truly mysterious.
Do you ever wish you could be completely and utterly alone? It is a daily dream for me.
(~smashfighter~ looks oddly familiar, but I can't put my finger on it... Did I dream about seeing ~smashfighter.isMale(him|her)~ fighting my teacher once? No... it couldn't be.)
I apologize if my reaction seemed disrespectful ~futa~, you simply caught me off guard is all.
Were you hoping to see my backside again, perchance? I suppose I wouldn't mind indulging you.
The interest in my posterior is more than a little embarrassing, but I suppose it is flattering all the same.
Oh! Though I don't see them, I should warn you, it's likely that Hubert's spies are watching from somewhere nearby. Only to ensure my safety of course, you can trust their discretion.
I quite enjoy tea, but my retainer, Hubert, is more partial to coffee. What about the rest of you?
If anybody finds a sketchbook lying about would you kindly return it to me? Just, whatever you do, don't look at the contents!
Things in reality are rarely black-and-white, people least of all. Try to fit everyone into categories of “good” and “bad”, or “friend” and “enemy”, and you’re liable to miss the full picture.
Have you heard from your grandfather lately, Petra? I trust he was pleased to hear that I'm open to negotiating the restoration Brigid's independence?
How have your studies been going Petra? I know you're working hard to master Fódlan's language, but remember not to your formal education slip.
I'm curious, do they have games like this back in Brigid, Petra?
Have you read any interesting books lately? For my part, I've been reading through a fascinating tome on monarch studies I got from Professor Byleth.
I’m in awe of how people from every walk of life are able to come together to play cards here. It truly is a marvel, don’t you think?
Linhardt once compared me to an overbearing mother. Is it so wrong that I try to push my classmates to reach their full potential?
A reasoned set of rules is essential for a prosperous society, but leaving traditions unchecked merely out of respect for their age will rot it from the inside out. Do you not agree ~royal~?
Hubert and I picked up poker as a way to practice reading each other's body language so we can immediately detect if something is amiss. One can never be too careful.
My classmate, Ferdinand, seems to have gotten it into his head that he's somehow my rival and won't stop challenging me to inane competitions. Do any of you know somebody like that?

The Imperial capital, Enbarr, is a magnificent city with over twelve hundred years of history. I'd be delighted to show you around if you ever visit... Assuming I can find the time amidst my duties, of course.
I was planning to put this off a bit longer... but... perhaps it's better if I just get it over with.
You know I can hear the both of you, yes? Is it really so hard to believe that I came because I was curious?
I'm standing right here, you know? I may not be the most forthcoming with my emotions but that doesn't mean I'm disinterested in a game like this.
The monastery? No. The church would rather limit my exposure to those outside the faith. I'm here for my own edification.
Here on church business? Hardly. The archbishop would likely be furious if she knew I was fraternizing with nonbelievers like this. I simply wanted to expand my horizons.
No. I'm here in my personal capacity. This game seemed a good opportunity to meet people with varying perspectives and to challenge myself.
None of the above, Meia. I simply thought this game could be a valuable experience; both for the opportunity to meet new people and the chance to push my boundaries.

I wasn't anticipating being the first casualty of the game.

Losing my undergarments already? This is certainly not how I foresaw this game going.

It occurs to me that your world would not be in the thrall of Crests as Fódlan is, ~player~. I envy that.
It occurs to me that other worlds would not be in the thrall of Crests as Fódlan is. I envy that.
